signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard establishes an acute leader-laggard divide across currency blocs. JPY leads the G10 complex with a 1-week average gain of +2.571% across 7 pairs, while NZD lags with an average decline of -1.640% across 4 pairs, driving the bilateral spread to an extreme 4.211%. JPY strength persists despite a heavy carry deficit against the G10 field, as hawkish BoJ rhetoric accelerates pricing for rate hikes. Conversely, the RBNZ faces diminishing domestic tailwinds while CFTC data shows NZD leveraged funds net short -23,004 contracts at the 4th percentile of its 52-week range (z = -1.81). NZD/USD trades at 0.5882, slipping below its 20-day moving average at 0.5910, reflecting broader kiwi vulnerability. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY, reflecting extreme bilateral divergence and flow unwinds. Catalyst: BoJ rate decision on 18 Sep. Risk: BoJ delivers an unexpectedly dovish hold that triggers a rapid carry-rebound squeeze.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Geopolitical Friction
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 155.95, having fallen -2.12% over the past week and settling beneath its technical cluster of the 20-day (158.96), 50-day (160.48), and 200-day (158.45) moving averages. Escalating naval incidents in the Strait of Hormuz layer persistent event risk into global markets, maintaining pressure on high-beta crosses despite low headline volatility with VIX at 14.5. The options market displays defensive positioning, with the 1-month 25-delta Risk Reversal at -2.54, signaling an intense put skew for USD weakness. Leveraged funds hold a substantial JPY net short of -111,297 contracts (2nd percentile, z = -2.18), creating severe asymmetric liquidation pressure if hawkish BoJ communication forces further short covering. Although the overnight OIS differential of SOFR 3.66% vs TONA 0.98% maintains a +268bp USD carry advantage, downside hedging demand completely dominates spot flow. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, pressured by aggressive options hedging and short-covering vulnerability. Catalyst: US CPI release ahead of the 16 Sep FOMC meeting. Risk: A sharp resurgence in US yields that forces the pair back above the 200-day moving average at 158.45.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Retail Sentiment Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7203, remaining elevated above its 20-day (0.7135), 50-day (0.7041), and 200-day (0.6988) moving averages. CFTC speculative positioning confirms that leveraged funds hold an extended net long of +50,250 contracts, sitting at the 94th percentile of the 52-week range (z = +1.79), with weekly adds stalling at -3,328 contracts. In sharp contrast, retail community sentiment is 90% short, generating a textbook institutional-versus-retail positioning divergence at historical boundaries. The pair enjoys a 69bp overnight carry advantage via AONIA 4.35% over SOFR 3.66%, while Saxo 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 7.2% against an HV30 of 6.0% (VRP +1.1%). BEER-model valuation registers spot as rich at z = +1.81σ against model fair value of 0.7081, warning that upside momentum is increasingly constrained by positioning exhaustion. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; crowded institutional positioning caps near-term upside extensions. Catalyst: FOMC rate decision on 16 Sep. Risk: Leveraged funds accelerate profit-taking, dragging spot below the 20-day moving average at 0.7135.
evidence: AONIA vs SOFR: +69bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Premium + Stalling Longs
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3517, slipping beneath its 20-day moving average of 1.3555 while holding above the 50-day SMA at 1.3456 and 200-day SMA at 1.3447. CBOE implied volatility on Cable is elevated at 11.0% against an HV30 of 4.7%, creating an extreme Volatility Risk Premium of +6.3% that reflects heavy institutional demand for tail-risk protection. Leveraged funds hold a crowded net long of +47,504 contracts at the 93rd percentile (z = +1.27), but liquidated -9,335 contracts in the latest reporting week, pointing to waning speculative enthusiasm. Meanwhile, the UK Economic Surprise Index has turned negative to -6.7, contrasting with relatively neutral carry where SONIA at 3.73% holds a nominal -7bp spread against SOFR at 3.66%. The combination of a large options hedging premium and position reduction warns that upward momentum is stalling. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; heavy options risk premium and stalling positioning cap upside. Catalyst: BoE policy decision on 17 Sep. Risk: A decisive daily close below the 50-day moving average at 1.3456 that triggers broad spec liquidation.
